chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'aba ibn Maymun, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And speak to the people good words,' he said: 'Speak good to the people and do not say anything except good, until you know what it is.'
ai.seo_question: How should one interpret the Quranic command to speak good to people according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) clarifies the Quranic command to 'speak good to people' by advising that one should speak good words and avoid anything else until one is certain of the goodness of what is being said. This highlights the ethical importance of verifying the virtue of one's speech before uttering it, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tahqiq* (verification) in daily conduct. The hadith underscores that 'goodness' is not merely polite speech but requires discernment to ensure the content aligns with divine approval.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Muawiya Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:83] and you shall speak to the people good words, said: ‘Speak good words to the people and do not be saying anything except for good until you learn what it is’.
en.sarwar: 9. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

About the words of Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, ‘. . . speak righteous words to people. . . .’ [2:83], the Imam said it means, ‘Do not say anything about a people except good until you actually learn all about it.’”
